programName: Wider Shoulders, Narrower Waist — V Shape
programDesc: A two-day home strength program for an intermediate trainee who wants a more athletic V-shaped silhouette: wider-looking upper back, fuller shoulders and balanced development of the chest, arms, legs and core. Do workout A on Tuesday and B on Thursday, allowing at least one recovery day between strength sessions. Begin with the short warm-up and a light preparation set before the first demanding lift. Finish most working sets with about 1–3 technically sound repetitions still possible. With dumbbells, first improve repetitions inside the prescribed range and only then increase weight; with bands, build repetitions before moving to a stronger resistance level. FitTimer suggests increases after completed exercises, but you decide whether the technique and recovery justify them. The displayed weights are starting reference values, not universal requirements: adjust them to real equipment and the remaining clean repetitions. Meaningful physique changes normally take months of consistent effort. Check performance, waist measurements and photos under similar conditions every four weeks. Training cannot remove fat from the waist alone. Recovery, regular activity, sleep and sensible nutrition all support results. If a joint hurts during a movement, reduce or stop that exercise and find an appropriate alternative.
plans: Thoracic rotation on all fours

Get on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Put the right hand behind your head. Turn the elbow toward the left hand, then rotate your chest toward the ceiling, keeping the pelvis steady. Return slowly and repeat before switching sides.
Avoid rotating your hips or arching only through the low back. Reduce the range if the movement shifts away from the upper back.
Light band pull-apart

Stand tall and hold a light band with both hands in front of the chest, palms down and slightly wider than shoulders. Pull the hands apart until the band approaches your chest. Keep elbows softly bent, then return with control.
If you shrug or lean backward, reduce resistance or widen the starting grip. This is a warm-up, not a maximal effort.
Bodyweight glute bridge

Lie on your back, bend your knees and place feet about hip-width apart beneath the knees. Exhale and lift your hips through the glutes until shoulders, hips and knees are aligned. Pause briefly, then lower with control without overextending the low back.
If your low back dominates, lift a little less. If the hamstrings cramp, move feet slightly closer to the hips.
Dead bug

Lie on your back with both arms above the chest and hips and knees bent about 90 degrees. Exhale while slowly lowering the right arm behind the head and the left leg away from you. Stop before the pelvis or low back loses control, return and alternate sides.
If the low back visibly lifts or the pelvis rocks, shorten the leg movement. Keep breathing rather than bracing with a breath hold.
Supported one-arm dumbbell row

Support your free hand on a firm sofa or bench and hinge forward with a neutral spine. Let the dumbbell hang with the palm facing the thigh. Pull the elbow back toward the hip until the hand approaches the waist, then lower slowly and allow a small forward reach of the shoulder blade. Complete both sides.
Do not rotate the torso to lift the weight. If you need to jerk the upper body, reduce the dumbbell load.
Incline push-up

Place hands on a firm raised surface, shoulder-width or slightly wider, fingers forward. Hold your body in one line from head to heels. Bend the elbows back and slightly outward to lower the chest toward the support; stop before losing trunk control and push back up. Choose support height by repetition quality.
If the lower back sags, tighten the glutes or raise the support. If elbows flare directly sideways, bring them slightly closer to the ribs.
Floor push-up

Place palms just wider than shoulders, fingers forward, and hold the body in one line from head to heels. Lower slowly with elbows approximately 30–45 degrees from the body. Stop before trunk control breaks, then push up smoothly. Start with fewer reps than you used on the incline.
If hips sag or elbows flare sharply, reduce reps or return to the raised-support version.
Dumbbell Romanian deadlift

Stand hip-width with two dumbbells against the front of the thighs, palms toward the legs. Soften the knees and push the hips backward, letting the torso hinge while the dumbbells stay close to the legs. Stop when the hamstrings stretch without rounding the spine. Return by driving the hips forward, without leaning back.
If it looks like a squat, reduce forward knee movement. If the back rounds, stop higher. Avoid overextending the back at the top.
Dumbbell lateral raise

Stand tall with dumbbells beside the outer thighs, palms facing inward and elbows slightly bent. Raise the arms out to the sides and a little forward to a comfortable height no higher than the shoulders. Do not deliberately turn thumbs downward. Lower under control for two to three seconds.
If you sway or shrug, reduce the weight. If the upper range creates shoulder discomfort, limit the height and reassess the load.
Straight-arm band pulldown

Secure the band to a solid high anchor in front of you. Face it, hold both ends, step back to light tension and hinge forward slightly. With elbows only softly bent, pull the hands down in an arc toward the front of the thighs. Keep the torso still and return slowly to a comfortable overhead height.
If you bend elbows to bring hands to the chest, this becomes a different row. If you arch the back, use less band tension.
Goblet squat

Stand with feet around shoulder width and toes slightly turned out. Hold one dumbbell vertically close to the chest by its upper plate, elbows pointing down. Bend at hips and knees to a comfortable squat depth while keeping the whole foot on the floor. Stand by pushing through the feet without arching back.
If heels rise, reduce depth and stabilize your stance. If knees collapse inward, guide them along the line of the toes.
Dumbbell curl

Stand with a dumbbell by each thigh, palms initially facing the body. Bend the elbows, gradually turning palms up while keeping elbows near the sides. Lift to a comfortable full curl, then lower slowly almost to straight arms. Keep the torso still.
If elbows travel forward or you lean back to lift, reduce the weight. Do not drop through the lowering phase.
Thoracic rotation on all fours

Get on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Put the right hand behind your head. Turn the elbow toward the left hand, then rotate your chest toward the ceiling, keeping the pelvis steady. Return slowly and repeat before switching sides.
Avoid rotating your hips or arching only through the low back. Reduce the range if the movement shifts away from the upper back.
Light band pull-apart

Stand tall and hold a light band with both hands in front of the chest, palms down and slightly wider than shoulders. Pull the hands apart until the band approaches your chest. Keep elbows softly bent, then return with control.
If you shrug or lean backward, reduce resistance or widen the starting grip. This is a warm-up, not a maximal effort.
Bodyweight squat

Stand with feet about hip-width or slightly wider and toes slightly turned out. Bend knees and hips, moving down and slightly back while the whole foot stays grounded. Descend to a comfortable depth and stand up without locking the lower back into an exaggerated arch.
If heels leave the floor, squat less deeply. If knees drift inward, guide them toward the toes.
High-anchored band lat pulldown

Attach the band securely above the head. Kneel or sit facing the anchor and take one end in each hand, arms reaching upward and forward, palms toward one another. Pull elbows down toward the sides until hands reach the upper ribs. Return slowly to an overhead reach without swinging the torso backward.
If the entire trunk falls backward, reduce band tension. If shoulders shoot toward the ears, decrease resistance and start more smoothly.
Neutral-grip dumbbell floor press

Lie on your back with bent knees and feet on the floor. Hold two dumbbells above the chest, palms facing each other and wrists straight. Lower the elbows beside the torso until the backs of the upper arms lightly touch the floor. Without bouncing, press back up over the chest.
If elbows flare directly to the sides or wrists bend backward, reset your grip. If you have to arch hard, reduce the load.
Static reverse split squat with dumbbells

Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Step back into a stable split stance with the feet on two parallel tracks rather than one narrow line. Keep the feet planted and bend both knees to descend with a slight natural forward trunk lean. Push through the front foot to stand. Complete both legs.
If the front knee collapses inward, track it over the toes. If balance is shaky, widen the stance or reduce load.
Standing dumbbell overhead press

Stand hip-width with a dumbbell near each shoulder, palms slightly turned toward each other and elbows a little forward. Brace gently through the abdomen and glutes, press upward along a comfortable path until arms are nearly straight, then lower to shoulder level. Keep the torso upright.
If the low back arches strongly or you lean back, lower the weight. If the movement produces shoulder discomfort, stop and use a comfortable option.
Dumbbell lateral raise

Stand tall with dumbbells beside the outer thighs, palms facing inward and elbows slightly bent. Raise the arms out to the sides and a little forward to a comfortable height no higher than the shoulders. Do not deliberately turn thumbs downward. Lower under control for two to three seconds.
If you sway or shrug, reduce the weight. If the upper range creates shoulder discomfort, limit the height and reassess the load.
Band face pull

Anchor the band around eye level, face the anchor and hold one end in each hand with palms facing inward. Step back to light tension and reach arms forward. Pull hands toward the temples while opening the elbows to roughly shoulder height, pause briefly and return smoothly. Keep the torso still.
If you lean back, use less resistance. If elbows head down toward the waist, this becomes a standard row rather than a rear-shoulder exercise.
Single-dumbbell weighted glute bridge

Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart. Place one dumbbell across the hips on a folded towel and hold it with both hands. Exhale and lift the hips using the glutes until shoulders, hips and knees align. Pause one second and lower smoothly without overextending the low back.
If the low back works more than the glutes, lift less and keep ribs controlled. If hamstrings cramp, bring feet slightly closer.
Band triceps pushdown

Attach the band securely overhead. Face the anchor, take an end in each hand, elbows tucked near the sides, forearms bent and palms facing inward. Straighten the elbows, bringing hands toward the thighs, then return the forearms upward slowly without moving the upper arms.
If elbows drift forward and back, reduce resistance. If you need to lean your whole body into the band, it is too heavy.
Kneeling side plank

Lie on one side with elbow under the shoulder and knees bent roughly 90 degrees. Press through the forearm and knees to lift hips into a line from shoulder to hip to knee. Put the free hand on the waist and breathe normally. Lower under control, then repeat on the other side.
If hips sag or drift backward, end the hold. If the shoulder shrugs up, reposition the elbow and shorten the duration.
Straight-leg side plank

Lie on one side with elbow below shoulder and legs straight, feet stacked or top foot slightly in front. Raise the hips until shoulder, pelvis and feet form one line, free hand on the waist. Breathe and keep hips steady, then lower with control and switch sides.
If hips sag or the trunk rotates toward the floor, shorten the hold. If the shoulder fatigues first, check the forearm position.
